solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Global network evolving wild breed? Wow!

indicators.note: something evolving changes its form, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naturalist marvels at a wild breed of animal that seems to be evolving before their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolving' rearranges WILD, BREED and WOW together into the three words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The web is the system of linked pages spanning the globe, a worldwide information network.

clue.text: Scent of whirling tornado

indicators.note: whirling spins things round, so the letters of tornado are mixed up

explanation.surface: A smell carried on a spinning storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' rearranges TORNADO.
explanation.definitionFit: An odorant is a substance giving off a smell, so it is a scent in the sense of something that smells.

clue.text: Tie flying cat? Oddly not true, in a way

indicators.note: taking the letters that are not in odd places leaves the even ones of flying cat
in a way says the word true is treated loosely, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a tale of a cat that flies, calling it untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly not' keeps the even letters of FLYING CAT, LIGA; 'in a way' rearranges TRUE to TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or thread used for binding, as a surgeon ties off a vessel.

clue.text: Morons primarily lacking intelligence

indicators.note: the opening part of the word is what goes missing, as primarily points to the start

parts.note: nitwits are stupid people, so morons

explanation.surface: Fools, above all, have no brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily lacking' drops NIT, the first part of NITWITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Your wits are your mental faculties, so wits is a plural noun for brains or cleverness.

clue.text: Go round the bend about flight compensation

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to dement is to drive or go mad, which is going round the bend
a fray is a fight or brawl; the clue's flight stands for that fight

explanation.surface: A passenger driven mad over the refund for a delayed flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets one word around the other. A fray is a fight, not a flight: the clue appears to carry a one-letter slip, and only 'fight' makes the parse work.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray is to pay costs, so defrayment is the payment that covers them, a compensation.

clue.text: Middle section sounds like rubbish

indicators.note: sounds like says a word is replaced by another spoken the same way

parts.note: waste is rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the middle of a piece of work as trash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' turns WASTE into its twin, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The waist is the narrow part of the body between ribs and hips, its central section.

clue.text: Colourful piece of cloth featuring fruit wrapped around dancer's head

indicators.note: the fruit is wrapped around the next piece, which sits inside it

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of dancer's

explanation.surface: A dancer wears a bright headscarf adorned with a fruit design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes D from dancer's, and 'wrapped around' sets it inside BANANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large brightly patterned handkerchief, often worn on the head or neck.

clue.text: Flour, milk, and eggs using non- Imperial measures for gatecrashers

parts.note: batter is the mixture of flour, milk and eggs used for pancakes
in, as in working in a medium, means using
grams are metric units, not the old imperial pounds and ounces

explanation.surface: A recipe for pancake batter, weighed out in metric units.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a recipe; 'gatecrashers' is the definition, taken literally as things that crash through gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Battering rams were heavy beams used to smash castle gates, so literally gatecrashers.

clue.text: Precautionary measure for the endless antisemitic cracks

indicators.note: cracks breaks the letters apart and puts them together again in a new order
endless means the last letter of the word goes

explanation.surface: A warning against bigoted wisecracks, framed as a safeguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts THE to TH; 'cracks' rearranges TH and ANTISEMITIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a stitch in time saves nine: a small fix now prevents bigger trouble later.

clue.text: In compensation, frog isn't mutating in a safe environment

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside the word for compensation

parts.note: amends are compensation, as in making amends

indicators.note: mutating means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim for damages over a frog that has not mutated in a protected habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutating' rearranges the letters of 'frog isn't', ignoring the apostrophe, and 'In' places that jumble inside the word for compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being among friends means you are with people you trust, a secure setting.

clue.text: See 10
For he's a jolly good fellow! Cheers!

definitions.text: For he's a jolly good fellow!
definitions.meaning: the ... of a gathering is the person everyone praises, as in the ... of the town
a drink to someone's health, with cheers as the cry

explanation.surface: A party sings a celebratory song and raises glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast names both the honoured person and the raised-glass salute, the two scenes the clue sketches.

clue.text: 'Jewish food in Muslim Art's a playful retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gallery mounts a playful retrospective of Muslim art and serves deli food.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters IMARTSAP sit across 'Muslim Art's a playful', and 'retrospective' reads them backwards. The opening quote mark is stray.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is cured, spiced beef, a staple of Jewish delicatessens.

clue.text: Queen's first person wholeheartedly held out for a change

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word held are left out of the long word
for a change says what remains is rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly resisted, giving their all for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H, E, L, D ('out') from WHOLEHEARTEDLY and rearrange the rest ('for a change').
explanation.definitionFit: The royal we is the monarch speaking of themself in the plural, a first-person pronoun used by a sovereign.

clue.text: Hunter lost in Italian capital should do this at the end of the holiday

definitions.text: should do this at the end of the holiday

indicators.note: in says the scrambled hunter goes inside the name of the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

indicators.note: lost suggests the word hunter has gone astray, its letters scrambled

explanation.surface: A hunter goes astray in Rome and needs to get back after the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges HUNTER to ETURNH, which goes 'in' ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to your house is what every traveller does when a vacation ends.

clue.text: Skinning plaice is not professional

indicators.note: skinning strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters of plaice go

explanation.surface: An amateur cook makes a hash of preparing a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinning' removes the outer letters of PLAICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to ordinary people rather than clergy or experts.

clue.text: Some polite, rational and cultured people

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of courteous, reasonable and cultivated folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'and cultured people' as definition; 'and' only links the wordplay to the definition, so the definition is 'cultured people'.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people interested in literature and the arts.

clue.text: Food provided by essentially economic dishes

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Thrifty dishes supply something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes NO from the centre of economic and SH from the centre of dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub, something to eat.

clue.text: Type of beach hotel one should stay out of

indicators.note: the word for one stays outside, so the letter for hotel goes within it

parts.note: single means one
Hotel is the radio code word for the letter H

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a certain seaside guest house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should stay out of' keeps SINGLE outside, with H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle beach is covered in small rounded pebbles rather than sand.

clue.text: French leader called, almost in panic, to get flowers

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: rang means called on the phone

indicators.note: almost means each of the two words stops just short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A French president phones in a frenzy to order a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims IN and PANIC to I and PANI, which follow F and RANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a tropical tree prized for its fragrant waxy blossoms.

clue.text: Ancient British church without its leader

indicators.note: the leader of the word church is its first letter, which is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: the Anglican church is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An old British congregation left without its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without its leader' takes C, the first letter of church, out of ANGLICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian relates to the Angles, the early Germanic settlers of eastern Britain.

clue.text: Start to rant continuously about one mode of transport

definitions.note: a singular phrase for a plural answer: railways as a system of travel

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of rant
about says the word for continuously goes around the next piece

parts.note: always means continuously
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles endlessly about the trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' gives R; 'about' puts ALWAYS around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Railways, taken together, are a system of travel by train.

clue.text: Women and children first, OK? On reflection, that's crazy

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the three words
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters of OK are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the rule of saving women and children first is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes WAC, and 'On reflection' turns OK into KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Had dinner, they say, around that time?

indicators.note: they say signals a word spoken that sounds the same as one spelt differently

parts.note: ate is had dinner

explanation.surface: Someone guesses when a meal was eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' swaps ATE for its sound-alike number; dinner at eight is the cliché behind the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight o'clock is a typical hour for an evening meal, the time the question hints at.

clue.text: Song from the outskirts of Amritsar, India

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A melody heard on the edge of an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outskirts of' gives AR from Amritsar and IA from India.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera.

clue.text: Oxymoronic writing?

parts.note: fiction that pairs the fantastic with the true-to-life sounds like a contradiction in terms

explanation.surface: A query about prose built on contradictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The genre's name joins two opposite ideas, the supernatural and the realistic, so the name itself is an oxymoron.
explanation.definitionFit: The literary style of García Márquez mixes fantasy into everyday realistic settings, a self-contradicting label.

clue.text: See 26
Absolutions for erstwhile old corrupt Etonians? That's about right

parts.note: ex means former, so erstwhile

indicators.note: about says the scrambled schoolboys go around the next letter
corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pardons granted to former pupils of an elite school who went bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges ETONIANS to NEATIONS, and 'about' puts it around R. Etonians are pupils of Eton, an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoneration clears someone of blame, so exonerations are acquittals or pardons.
